title: J.D. Patterson — the Fife family and the ground it stood on (side B)
subtitle: Bethel Presbyterian Church, Historical Room — oral history
date_source: Side B carries no date of its own: it opens mid-question, 'What was his first name? Was it Samuel?', continuing the conversation on Side A, and is dated from that side's opening 'April 20th'. The year is established from the typescript of the same interview (1979-04-20-jd-patterson-documents, title page: 'Oral interview with Mr. J. D. Patterson, April 20, 1979'). The folder id keeps the unknown- prefix this item was queued under.

provenance.collection: Bethel Presbyterian Church — Historical Room oral histories
provenance.capture_notes: One cassette side, ALAC 48 kHz stereo 16-bit, 31:06.240. Received as 'JD Patterson Side B.m4a' in the collection root and renamed to the archive stem without touching the samples. The sound runs to 30:52 and the side ends with 'Thank you.' at 31:04.8; nothing was cropped. A second SRT in this folder, transcript-both-sides.srt, puts both sides on one clock by offsetting this side by 2156.288 s, Side A's duration.

speakers.label: JD
speakers.name: James Douglass Patterson
speakers.note: Continues from Side A; the Fife, Hultz, Boyer and Espy families of Upper St. Clair and Bethel.

speakers.label: JUNE
speakers.name: June Ellington
speakers.note: Labelled only where her words are unambiguous (a question, a name-check, an aside to the room); her one-word acknowledgements stay under JD because no diarisation separates them.

speakers.label: ANNOUNCEMENT

speakers.note: The closing ownership statement: 'This is a recording of oral history to be the property of Upper St. Clair Historical Society and will only be used by non-profit' - neither speaker.
